content.title: About
content.content: Garlic bread is a fragrant loaf, usually made from a baguette or ciabatta, brushed with a mixture of butter, minced garlic, herbs, and sometimes cheese. It is popular as a snack or side dish for soups, pasta, and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Garlic bread is often served in Italian restaurants alongside pasta.
There are many variations, including versions with Parmesan, mozzarella, or spicy herbs.
Garlic enhances flavor perception and has antibacterial properties.
The traditional recipe calls for baking the bread until the crust turns golden.
In some countries, garlic bread is served as small bite‑size pieces called “grissini.”

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Garlic contains allicin and other compounds that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Regular consumption of garlic may strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Cholesterol reduction
items.content: Studies suggest garlic can help lower “bad” LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Improved digestion
items.content: Garlic stimulates gastric juice production, aiding nutrient absorption.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: It provides vitamin B6, important for protein metabolism.

items.title: Garlic allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as swelling or rash.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: Large amounts of raw garlic can cause heartburn or discomfort.

items.title: Breath odor
items.content: Garlic breath can linger for several hours after eating.

items.title: Interaction with medications
items.content: Garlic may enhance the effect of anticoagulants, so caution is advised for those on blood thinners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice a baguette, spread a mixture of butter, minced garlic, and herbs, then bake until golden. Serve hot, cutting into serving pieces. Optionally sprinkle grated cheese a few minutes before the end of baking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best consumed within 1‑2 days. Keep in an airtight container at room temperature to retain crust crispness. For longer storage, freeze in bags and reheat in the oven before serving.
